@dzianisv thanks for the thorough review — and agreed on all of it. I've acted on both of your recommendations:

**(1) Nested-spawning first** is up as **#32301** — the #23091/#13715 fixes (ask-routing-to-root) plus the four guardrails, small and reviewable on its own, green CI, mergeable. Exactly the "land this first, it's wanted regardless" piece.

**(2) The workflow subsystem** is now a stacked split into focused, independently-reviewable PRs:
- #32390 — engine-core (the 4,810-line `workflow.ts` modularized into schema/errors/types + barrel)
- #32392 — server routes + SDK
- #32393 — TUI
- #32394 — app + desktop
- #32395 — `ctx.tool(...)` + plugin registration
- #32396 — docs

Per your note about generated churn, the regenerated SDK/openapi is isolated in **#32392** rather than spread across the diff; each PR is workflow-only (unrelated drift dropped). Would love to see this reviewed and landed soon. Thanks for the great work!

I have the same issue since 1.16.0.
It seems like the modified files list is not shown at all anymore.

This looks like it shares a root cause with [#17622](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/issues/17622), which now has a fix up in [#32410](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/32410).

I came at it from the server/main isolate rather than Windows, but the retained strings I found match what you described. They were full per-file unified diffs (`Index: <file>` ... `@@`), held alive through `summary.diffs`. The cause is that `SessionSummary.summarize()` stored the full `patch` text from `Snapshot.diffFull()` on each user message's `info.summary.diffs`, which stays in the hydrated message list and gets persisted into `message.data`. On a session that keeps editing the same large file, every turn retains another full copy of that file's contents, so in my snapshot I saw 8 live copies of the same 2.7 MB diff. That fits both your "repeated retained strings that look like session message artifacts" observation and the way reopening amplifies it, since reopen rehydrates all of those rows.

The fix in [#32410](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/32410) stops `summarize()` from keeping the patch text at all (it holds only file, status, and line-count metadata now) and recomputes the full diff on demand in `diff()` when something actually needs it. After the change my server snapshot retained zero of those file-diff copies. I should be upfront that this is the server-side source, so it may not fully cover any retention you saw living purely in the TUI isolate on Windows, but it removes the largest accumulating piece that gets rehydrated on reopen.

One concrete source of long-session memory growth now has a fix up in [#32410](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/32410), which closes [#17622](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/issues/17622).

`SessionSummary.summarize()` was storing the full per-file diff text from `Snapshot.diffFull()` on each user message's `info.summary.diffs`. That stays in the hydrated message list and gets persisted into `message.data`, so a session that repeatedly edits the same large file keeps a fresh full copy of that file's contents every turn. A server heap snapshot showed 8 live copies of one 2.7 MB diff. The fix keeps only lightweight metadata (file, status, line counts) and recomputes the full diff on demand, after which none of those copies are retained.

Same crash here on **OpenCode Desktop v1.17.7** — newer than the v1.15.10 in this report, so the issue is **still present on the latest build**.

On my side the minidump points the fault at the bundled native watcher `@parcel/watcher-win32-x64\watcher.node`, matching the upstream bug `parcel-bundler/watcher#250` (`std::regex_match` stack overflow on long paths when a glob-ignore option is used). I filed the root-cause details separately in #32443.

One observation that narrows the trigger: the crash only fires for long paths created **inside the directories / workspaces the watcher is actually scanning**. Long-named files written to temporary scratch locations *outside* the watched tree (e.g. `%TEMP%`) do **not** crash the sidecar. This is consistent with the fault being in the watcher's path/glob regex matching rather than in generic file I/O — only paths that the watcher enumerates reach the crashing code.
